name: San Tan Valley
seo_title: San Tan Valley Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 4 Events, 4 Free
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in San Tan Valley, AZ: Loop of Lights, Slices with Santa, the Dust Bowl Christmas Light Parade and a live nativity on Christmas Eve.
lede: San Tan Valley celebrates Christmas with a resident-run neighborhood light walk, a golf cart and side-by-side light parade and Santa visits hosted by local businesses.
celebrates: San Tan Valley's best-known tradition is Loop of Lights, a neighborhood walk in Pecan Creek South where residents decorate their homes and the walk is always free. Around it, the community calendar at SanTanValley.com lists Santa visits at Geno's Giant Slice, the Dust Bowl Christmas Light Parade where riders decorate side-by-sides, motorcycles, dirt bikes and horses, and a live nativity at Berean Baptist Church on Christmas Eve. Families also drive to nearby Queen Creek for Christmas at Schnepf Farms and to SanTan Village in Gilbert for tree lighting and Santa.
lastyear: In December 2025, SanTanValley.com wrote that Loop of Lights was lighting up the neighborhood once again, calling it one of San Tan Valley's most cherished holiday traditions. The Loop's own Facebook page listed a Hot Cocoa and the Grinch event that season, and the Loop's site lists the San Tan Valley Veteran Center under its 2025 giving. Visitors parked at Ellsworth Elementary and walked the Loop, where Santa appears on weekends and residents run cocoa and popcorn booths.
facts: Loop of Lights started in 2007, and the site says Rhett Homan imagined a Christmas light walk that would pull neighbors into the street and keep them there. It is not an HOA production: residents volunteer their time, their yards and their electricity. A calendar listing from the Loop's 12th season counted over 120 homes in the display. Extras such as choo-choo rides, light wands at the Bumble House, Santa photos and cocoa ask for a donation, and the proceeds go to the Loop's charity of the year.
trains: San Tan Valley's own train fun is at Loop of Lights, where the host lists choo-choo rides as a donation extra. For a longer ride, the Superstition Scenic Narrow Gauge Railroad at Goldfield Ghost Town in Apache Junction runs a 20-minute narrated loop daily, and the Mesa Santa Express carries families on a decorated Valley Metro light rail car each December. The Arizona Railway Museum in Chandler and the Phoenix Trolley Museum are the nearest railroad museums.

faq: Yes. The Loop of Lights site says it is always free to walk the displays. Some extras, such as choo-choo rides, light wands at the Bumble House, Santa photos and cocoa, ask for a donation or a few dollars, and the proceeds go to the Loop's charity of the year.
Where do you park for Loop of Lights?

The Loop of Lights site says to park at Ellsworth Elementary and walk the Loop in Pecan Creek South, at 38454 N Carolina Ave. The roads are barricaded to residents, and bikes, wagons, side-by-sides and horse-drawn carriages are welcome, as long as animals are cleaned up after.
When did Loop of Lights start?

The Loop's site says the Christmas light walk started in 2007, when Rhett Homan imagined a walk that would pull neighbors into the street and keep them there. It is run by residents, not an HOA, who volunteer their time, their yards and their electricity.
Where can kids meet Santa in San Tan Valley?

Santa wanders Loop of Lights on weekends in December, and Geno's Giant Slice hosts Slices with Santa in its parking lot. SanTan Village in nearby Gilbert and Christmas at Schnepf Farms in Queen Creek also have Santa visits.
Is there a train ride near San Tan Valley?

Loop of Lights lists choo-choo rides as a donation extra. The Superstition Scenic Narrow Gauge Railroad in Apache Junction runs a 20-minute narrated loop around Goldfield Ghost Town, and Christmas at Schnepf Farms in Queen Creek has the Illumination Express train ride.

intro_html:
Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in San Tan Valley for 2026, and here is what he found: 4 family events, 4 of them free. The magic runs from December 1 through December 31 (Loop of Lights STV), with Slices with Santa at Geno's Giant Slice (December 6), the Dust Bowl Christmas Light Parade (December 11) and a Live Christmas Nativity at Berean Baptist Church (December 24) along the way. We check every date on the host's own website, and each listing links straight there.
